exercises.title: Part 1 · 1
exercises.prompt: Where do you go to get a haircut?

exercises.title: Part 1 · 2
exercises.prompt: Have you changed your hairstyle recently?

exercises.title: Part 1 · 3
exercises.prompt: Would you ever change the colour of your hair?

exercises.title: Part 1 · 4
exercises.prompt: Do you enjoy going to the hairdresser/barber?

exercises.title: Part 2 · 1
exercises.prompt: Describe a time when you used information for tourists, for example from a guidebook or online. You should say: where you got this information; what place this information was about; what information you got; and explain whether this information was very helpful for you.

exercises.title: Part 3 · 1
exercises.prompt: What are the most popular kinds of holidays for people from your country to go on?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 2
exercises.prompt: Do you think most people prefer to have a holiday abroad rather than in their own country?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 3
exercises.prompt: Why do some people want to do absolutely nothing when they go away on holiday?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 4
exercises.prompt: What are the kinds of tourist attraction that visitors to your country like to see?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 5
exercises.prompt: Do you think tourist attractions such as museums should be free for local people to visit?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 6
exercises.prompt: What can make a tourist attraction disappointing for visitors?

images.alt: Cambridge IELTS 21 Test 2 Speaking original page

exercises.title: Part 1 · 1
exercises.prompt: How well do you know the capital city of your country?

exercises.title: Part 1 · 2
exercises.prompt: Do you think cities are exciting places to live?

exercises.title: Part 1 · 3
exercises.prompt: Why do some people dislike living in a city?

exercises.title: Part 1 · 4
exercises.prompt: If you could visit any city in the world, where would you go?

exercises.title: Part 2 · 1
exercises.prompt: Describe a time when you read or heard something that you thought was not true. You should say: where you read/heard this; what you read/heard; why you thought it was not true; and explain how you felt about reading/hearing this thing that you thought was not true.

exercises.title: Part 3 · 1
exercises.prompt: Do you think children are more honest than adults?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 2
exercises.prompt: Why do adults tell children it's important to be honest?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 3
exercises.prompt: Do you think there are sometimes good reasons for adults not to tell children the truth?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 4
exercises.prompt: Are there any claims in advertisements that are sometimes not true?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 5
exercises.prompt: Why do people still buy things even when they know advertisements aren't completely accurate?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 6
exercises.prompt: Do you think advertisements that are dishonest should be banned?

images.alt: Cambridge IELTS 21 Test 3 Speaking original page

exercises.title: Part 1 · 1
exercises.prompt: When you go shopping, do you usually pay for things by cash or by card?

exercises.title: Part 1 · 2
exercises.prompt: Are you generally careful about how much money you spend?

exercises.title: Part 1 · 3
exercises.prompt: Have you ever spent money on something you didn't need?

exercises.title: Part 1 · 4
exercises.prompt: How important is it to you to save money for the future?

exercises.title: Part 2 · 1
exercises.prompt: Describe an interesting garden or park you have seen. You should say: where this garden or park is; how big it is; what you saw in this garden/park; and explain why you think this garden/park is interesting.

exercises.title: Part 3 · 1
exercises.prompt: What are the advantages of having a home with a garden?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 2
exercises.prompt: How could people living in apartment blocks grow plants and vegetables?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 3
exercises.prompt: How interested are people in your country in TV shows and magazines about gardens?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 4
exercises.prompt: Do you think that gardening is a hobby mainly for older people?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 5
exercises.prompt: What are the benefits for people of gardening as a hobby?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 6
exercises.prompt: Will gardening be a more popular hobby in the future?

images.alt: Cambridge IELTS 21 Test 4 Speaking original page

exercises.title: Part 1 · 1
exercises.prompt: When do you usually eat bread?

exercises.title: Part 1 · 2
exercises.prompt: How important is bread in your culture?

exercises.title: Part 1 · 3
exercises.prompt: Have you tried any kinds of bread from other countries?

exercises.title: Part 1 · 4
exercises.prompt: Would you be interested in learning how to make bread?

exercises.title: Part 2 · 1
exercises.prompt: Describe a person you know who is very competitive. You should say: who this person is; what this person is competitive about; how successful this person is; and explain why you think this person is so competitive.

exercises.title: Part 3 · 1
exercises.prompt: What kinds of competitions do people like to enter in your country?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 2
exercises.prompt: What do you think is the best kind of prize to win in a competition?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 3
exercises.prompt: Why do people like watching quiz shows and other competitions on TV?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 4
exercises.prompt: How important is it to be very competitive at sport?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 5
exercises.prompt: Do you think sportspeople perform better when they play against competitors who are stronger than they are?

exercises.title: Part 3 · 6
exercises.prompt: Why do some people think that taking part in sport is more important than winning?
